brief: An 8-second donut chart: four segments, 40% 'Rent', 25% 'Food', 20% 'Travel' and 15% 'Other', each in a distinct color, grow clockwise one after another; each segment gets its label and percentage placed outside the ring; the total '$2,400' counts up from $0 in the center.
checks: The video shows a centered donut chart (a ring with a hole).
The chart is divided into exactly four visible segments.
The four segments correspond to the correct percentages and labels: the largest (~40%) is labeled “Rent 40%”, the next (~25%) “Food 25%”, then (~20%) “Travel 20%”, then (~15%) “Other 15%”.
Each segment uses a distinctly different color (no two segments share the same hue).
The segments appear (grow) in clockwise order, one after another, with each segment finishing its growth before the next begins.
For each segment, its label and percentage are placed outside the ring, adjacent to that segment, and remain visible after the segment finishes growing.
The central numeric total starts at $0 and counts up smoothly to $2,400 by the end of the video.
All text (labels, percentages, central total) is at least about one‑tenth of the frame height high and has high contrast against its background.
No graphic or text touches or crosses the outer frame edge; there is a clear margin around the composition.
Animations (segment growth, label appearance, number count‑up) use ease‑in/ease‑out timing rather than moving at a constant speed.
There is meaningful motion or change in every second of the video (no dead air), and nothing appears before the first half‑second has elapsed.
The final composition holds still for at least half a second before the video ends, and the picture fills the whole frame with no black bars, borders, or hard‑edged vignettes.
